transcript.text: dryer drum wont turn but i can here it running, hotpiont. clothes just sit there

If the dryer is running but the drum stays still, the most likely cause is the drive belt having slipped off or snapped. Less commonly, the drum is binding because of a worn support/bearing or an item caught in it; if it only hums rather than properly running, the motor or its start capacitor is possible. Switch it off and unplug it, empty the drum, then turn the drum slowly by hand. Tell me whether it feels stiff or stuck, or spins unusually freely with little resistance. Avoid using it until this is sorted, as stationary clothes can overheat.
unplugged and turned the drum by hand and it spins really easy almost no resistance. heard a twang/thud yesterday mid cycle then just the motor sound and a slight rubber smell at the time

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. That pattern points very strongly to a snapped or thrown-off drum drive belt: the twang/thud was likely the belt failing, the motor can still be heard, and the drum now turns with almost no resistance. The slight rubber smell also fits a slipping or damaged belt; the tension/jockey pulley may have contributed and should be inspected at the same time. Do not use the dryer again. It needs a qualified appliance engineer to inspect the belt, pulley and motor area, and remove any rubber debris or lint buildup before it is put back into service. This is normally a repairable mechanical fault, rather than needing a new dryer.

candidates: Drive belt has come off or snapped (high)
Drum jammed or worn drum support/bearing (medium)
